quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on the most difficult player he defended in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: Russell Westbrook was the most difficult player I had to defend in the league at that time.

text_blocks.speaker: Ricardo Vega
text_blocks.text: In the NBA, you played the point guard position against many players who were also horses. You faced Rayon Rondo, Chris Paul. Who was that player, Gravy, that you said, no, no, no, that guy was the most difficult in the league at that time?

text_blocks.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
text_blocks.text: The player I always found difficult to defend, the one I was always very aware of, because he was an indomitable, unpredictable style of player, was Russell Westbrook. It was impressive how this guy destabilized a defense.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on Russell Westbrook's rebounding dominance as a point guard
quotes.excerpt: Russell Westbrook probably has more offensive rebounds in the history of the point guard position in the NBA.
quotes.quote: Russell Westbrook is probably one of the point guards or guards who went to the offensive rebound the most. In terms of statistics, he has to have more offensive rebounds in the history of the point guard position in the NBA. Because when you are a point guard, you usually stay in the defensive balance. When your teammate shoots, you go to the defensive balance. Not this guy. He goes to the rim, and he goes up like a rainbow. And you know, when you do that, the guy is flying around and boom, he slams it in your face.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Russell Westbrook es probablemente uno de los point guards o bases que más fue al rebote ofensivo. En números, en estadísticas, tiene que tener más rebotes ofensivos en la historia de la posición de base en la NBA. Porque cuando tú eres base, tú usualmente te quedas en el balance defensivo. Cuando tu compañero lanza, tú vas al balance defensivo. No este tipo. Él va al aro y él sale volando como un arcoíris. Y tú sabes, cuando tú haces así, el tipo está volando por acá y boom, te la clava en la cara.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on his professional relationship with Jose Manuel Calderon
quotes.excerpt: I respect Jose Manuel Calderon, I love him. I think he's a great professional.
quotes.quote: Jose Manuel Calderon. Once we were in Spain playing Venezuela against Spain and I was in college and he kind of treated me like, you know, you're too rookie, you're still in college. And I kept that in my head. And after, when I played in Toronto, he was in Detroit. Every time I went to Toronto, he didn't know I had a mind with him. Look, I respect Calderon, I respect him, I love him. I think he's a great professional. But I always had that little chip on my shoulder.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: José Manuel Calderón. Una vez estamos en España jugando Venezuela contra España y yo estaba en la universidad y él como que me trató de, tú sabes, estás muy novato, todavía estás en college. Y yo me quedé con eso. Y después cuando yo jugaba en Toronto, él estaba en Detroit. Cada vez que él iba para Toronto, él no sabía que yo tenía una una mente con él. Ojo, lo respeto a Calderón, lo respeto, lo quiero. Yo creo que es un gran profesional. Pero yo siempre me quedé con eso.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on the evolution of the modern NBA center
quotes.excerpt: Today a center initiates an offense. Today a center hits four or five triples.
quotes.quote: Today a center initiates an offense. Today a center hits four or five triples. Today a center not only initiates an offense, he plays a pick-and-roll with him having the ball in his hand. When did you see that? You didn't see a Shaquille O'Neal outside the key. So the basketball today is a different basketball, a modern basketball, that some fans like or like, and others don't.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Hoy un centro inicia una ofensiva. Hoy un centro te mete cuatro o cinco triples. Hoy un centro no solo te inicia una ofensiva, te juega un pick and roll con él teniendo la bola en la mano. ¿Cuándo tú veías eso? Tú no veías un Shaquille O'Neal fuera de la llave. Entonces el baloncesto hoy es un baloncesto distinto, un baloncesto moderno, que a ciertos fanáticos les apetece o les gusta y a otros no.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on Sam Presti as the best NBA executive
quotes.excerpt: For me, the best president and general manager in the NBA is Sam Presti.
quotes.quote: For me, the best president and general manager in the NBA is Sam Presti. If I didn't mention him, I would stop. Because look at what he does. The basketball, the NBA, is a job more than office-based. These guys read numbers, these guys match numbers, these guys measure, and they see advanced statistics. How does this player work with this player? How does he shoot from the corner? Does he dribble with his left? When he dribbles with his left, what does he do? How much money does this one make? We can change these two to match the money here. And how does he do that? He had to leave three important players. He had to leave them and you think he did it wrong. And the year that comes, the guy from here to 2030, I think he has 27 second-round picks. So the guy is playing Monopoly. He is playing Monopoly.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Para mí tiene que estar este muchacho de Oklahoma, Sam Presti. Si no mencionabas a ese, me paraba. Porque mira lo que él hace. El baloncesto, la NBA, es un trabajo más que oficinario. Estos tipos leen números, estos tipos machean números, estos tipos miden y ven estadísticas avanzadas. ¿Cómo funciona este jugador con este jugador? ¿Cómo lanza desde la esquina? ¿Dribla con la izquierda? Cuando dribla con la izquierda, ¿qué hace? ¿Cuánto dinero gana este? Podemos cambiar estos dos para machear el dinero aquí. ¿Y cómo hace eso? Él tuvo que dejar tres jugadores importantes. Él tuvo que dejarlos y tú piensas que lo hizo mal. Y el año que viene, el tipo de aquí al 2030, creo que tiene 27 escogencias de segunda ronda. Entonces el tipo está jugando Monopoly. Él está jugando Monopoly.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on Kobe Bryant's legacy and the Lakers' dynasty
quotes.excerpt: If Kobe Bryant hadn't been stubborn, it would have been a hegemony of more than five rings.
quotes.quote: If Kobe Bryant hadn't been stubborn with Kobe, Kobe with him, it would have been a hegemony of more than five rings. More than five rings. Because he had the perimeter and he had the key covered. And he was an unstoppable type. The type grabbed, he would throw himself back, a butt, he would turn around and boom, with both hands. So how do you stop that?
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Si él no se hubiese puesto testarudo con Kobe, ni Kobe con él, eso hubiese sido una hegemonía de más de cinco más de cinco anillos. Más de cinco anillos. Porque tenía el perímetro y tenía la llave cubierta. Y él era un tipo imparable. El tipo la agarraba, se echaba para atrás, culazo, se volteaba y boom, con las dos manos. Entonces, ¿cómo tú parabas eso?

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on the high number of role players in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: There are 420 players who are role players and earn millions of dollars for a role.
quotes.quote: How many players exist in the NBA? 460 something players. Tell me you, how many superstars are in the league today? There have to be between 10 or 15. 10 or 15. I'll give you 15. Superstars. How many stars? 25. We have 40. You take 460 minus 40, that gives you 420 players, right? They are 420 players. This is for all those young people who want to play professional and who want to reach the NBA. They are 420 players who are role players and earn millions of dollars for a role.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: ¿Cuántos jugadores existen en la NBA? 460 y pico de jugadores. Díganme ustedes, ¿cuántas superestrellas hay en la liga hoy? Tienen que haber entre 10 o 15. 10 o 15. Te voy a dar 15. Superestrellas. ¿Cuántas estrellas? 25. Tenemos 40. Tú quitas 460 menos 40, te da 420 jugadores, ¿verdad? Son 420 jugadores. Esto es para todos esos jóvenes que quieren jugar profesional y que quieren llegar a la NBA. Son 420 jugadores que son jugadores de rol y cobran millones de dólares por un rol.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on Al Horford's role in the Celtics' success
quotes.excerpt: Al Horford's role was one thing: rest Jalen Brunson and keep the game there.
quotes.quote: What was the role of Al Horford? One thing: rest Jalen Brunson and keep the game there. That was the role. That is a role. And for that, they pay him millions of dollars and he won a title. In the city probably most important of all the United States. So that is the love to the game, that is the understanding to the game.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: ¿Cuál era el rol de Al Horford? uno solo: descansar a Jalen Brunson y mantener el juego ahí. Ese era el rol. Eso es un rol. Y por eso a él le pagan millones de dólares y se ganó un título. En la ciudad probablemente más importante de todos los Estados Unidos. Entonces ese es el amor al juego, ese es el entendimiento al juego.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on the importance of experience for young athletes
quotes.excerpt: Experience is key, guys. When you have experience in any field, you stand out.
quotes.quote: Experience is key, guys. When you have experience in any field, you stand out, because you know the times, there is no despair, you know when to put turbo, when not, you know when to go fast and when to go slow, you know when you change the pace, you know what you are going to put, you know that all that is key.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: La experiencia es clave, muchachos. Cuando tú tienes experiencia en cualquier rubro, tú te destacas, porque sabes los tiempos, no hay desespero, sabes cuándo meter turbo, cuándo no, sabes cuándo ir rápido y cuándo ir lento, sabes cuándo es cambias el pace, sabes qué te vas a poner, sabes que todo eso es clave.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on Victor Wembanyama as the face of the NBA
quotes.excerpt: The face of the NBA, I say it here, will be Victor Wembanyama.
quotes.quote: I'm in negotiations with NBC Telemundo to renew, I already renewed with Monumental Sports Network, it's being talked about with another big network, because now you don't sign exclusivity, now you sign amount of games, so that gives you repetitions. And I think the future is unlimited. And as I told you, I'm in a moment in my life right now that I recovered my years of injury and now I find a satisfaction in what I do. And part of, because I have to mention it, is Jim Family. Jim Family is a league in Miami, for me the best league in Miami, led by two people I love who are my brothers, which is Christian Samboy, aka Sugar, Jesus Galicia, aka Baron Davis. It has been a league that has caught me and has given me a respect that many times in my own country they don't give me.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Ahorita estoy en negociaciones con NBC Telemundo para renovar, ya renové con Monumental Sports Network, se está hablando con otro network grande, porque ahora tú no firmas exclusividad, ahora tú firmas cantidad de juegos, entonces eso te da repeticiones. Y yo creo que el futuro es ilimitado. Y como les dije, estoy en un momento de mi vida ahorita que recuperé mis años de lesión y ahora sí encuentro una satisfacción a lo que hago. Y parte de, porque hay que mencionarlo, es Jim Family. Jim Family es una liga en Miami, para mí la mejor liga en Miami, liderada por dos personas que amo que son mis hermanos, que es Christian Samboy, aka Sugar, Jesús Galicia, aka Barón Davis. Ha sido una liga que me ha atrapado y me ha dado un respeto que muchas veces en mi propio país no me lo dan.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on the importance of team chemistry and role players
quotes.excerpt: There are other players of the generational relief that have a little more charisma than Wembanyama.
quotes.quote: There are other players of the generational relief that have a little more charisma than Wembanyama, for example, there you have Anthony Edwards, who is a type that has a lot of fan base. And they are types that are betting to be they the relief. So I bet that Anthony Edwards has to be sitting in his house, analyzing and feeling that he can be the relief of LeBron.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Hay otros jugadores del relevo generacional que tienen un poquito más de carisma que Wembanyama, por ejemplo, ahí tú tienes a Anthony Edwards, que es un tipo que tiene mucha fanaticada. Y son tipos que están apostando a ser ellos el relevo. O sea, yo te apuesto que Anthony Edwards tiene que estar sentado en su casa, analizando y sintiendo que él puede ser el relevo de LeBron.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on the impact of his trade to Toronto
quotes.excerpt: I was changed a December 24 from Sacramento to Toronto, I buying the baby Jesus for my children.
quotes.quote: If they changed me a December 24 from Sacramento to Toronto, I buying the baby Jesus for my children. I received a call, I with my daughter in my hand, my little son buying gifts for Christmas. You are changed. You are changed. There nobody said anything. And eye, I was a low-profile player, because here you have to speak clearly, and I always knew my role. So when you talk about Kevin Durant and him deciding his destiny, why he doesn't have the right? Because I have six operations in my right ankle, and today I do a lot of work with the NBA, but if not, the people forget you.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Si a mí me cambiaron un 24 de diciembre de Sacramento a Toronto, yo comprándole el niño Jesús a mis hijos. Yo recibí una llamada, yo con mi hija en la mano, mi hijo chiquito comprando regalos de Navidad. Usted está cambiado. Usted está cambiado. Ahí nadie dijo nada. Y ojo, yo era un jugador de bajo perfil, porque aquí hay que hablar claro, y yo siempre supe mi rol. Entonces cuando tú hablas de Kevin Durant y él decidir su destino, ¿por qué él no tiene el derecho? Porque yo tengo seis operaciones en mi tobillo derecho, y hoy en día sí trabajo mucho con la NBA, pero si no, la gente te olvida.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on LeBron James' influence on the NBA
quotes.excerpt: You are going to tell me that LeBron James is not the one who sends in the NBA?
quotes.quote: You are going to tell me that LeBron James is not the one who sends in the NBA? Far, far. And what did the commissioner say? The commissioner said, I am waiting for LeBron to take the decision because, man, look, we have television contracts that we haven't put, the game calendar hasn't come out. Brother, all the teams stopped because we don't know which team you are going to. They can't trade, they can't conform their teams. So, nobody says anything about that. The owner of the league.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Ustedes me van a decir a mí que LeBron James no es el que manda en la NBA? Claro, lejos. ¿Y qué dijo el comisionado? El comisionado dijo, yo estoy esperando a LeBron que tome la decisión porque, pana, mira, tenemos contratos de televisión que no hemos puesto, el calendario de juego no ha salido. Brother, todos los equipos parados porque no sabemos para qué equipo vas. No pueden cambiar, no pueden conformar sus equipos. Entonces, nadie dice nada de eso. El dueño de la liga.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on his trade to Toronto and the role of Masai Ujiri
quotes.excerpt: I arrive in Toronto because Masai Ujiri was one of the scouts of Denver Nuggets.
quotes.quote: I arrive in Toronto because Masai Ujiri was one of the scouts of Denver Nuggets when I went to Basketball Without Borders in Brazil. That was in a military base. Masai Ujiri, who is after that makes Toronto champion with his leadership. He takes me there because he knows me and he tells me, you are going to be the starting point guard of the team because I am going to send Kyle Lowry to New York. You remember in that time that they change me to Toronto, there was that rumor that Kyle Lowry was going to New York.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Yo llego a Toronto porque Masai Ujiri fue uno de los scouts de Denver Nuggets cuando yo fui al baloncesto sin fronteras en Brasil. Eso fue en una base militar. Masai Ujiri, que es después hace a Toronto campeón con su dirigencia. Él me lleva allá porque me conoce y me dice, vas a ser el piloto abridor del equipo porque voy a mandar a Kyle Lowry para Nueva York. ¿Se acuerdan en ese tiempo que me cambian a mí para Toronto, había ese rumor de que Kyle Lowry iba para Nueva York.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on the chemistry of the Toronto Raptors roster
quotes.excerpt: We won 10 games in a row and the same players that we arrived in Toronto brought a different energy.
quotes.quote: Result and happens that we go, Patrick Patterson, Chuck Hayes, we are in Sacramento, and I. I think one more. Yes. When we arrived in Toronto, everything clicked. We won 10 games in a row and the same players that we arrived in Toronto, as we brought a different energy, a different vibe and with desire to win, we talked with Masai and told him, don't change a thing. Because Kado is the precursor and protagonist of the band. He was the backman, DeMar DeRozan was the Robin. And what we came behind were some big books, dwarfs that we did chorus to him. And as there was a good chemistry, they finish leaving the team.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Resulta y acontece que vamos, Patrick Patterson, Chuck Hayes, estamos en Sacramento, y yo. Creo que uno más. Sí. Cuando llegamos nosotros a Toronto, todo cliqueó. Ganamos 10 juegos seguidos y los mismos jugadores que llegamos a Toronto, como trajimos una energía distinta, una vibra distinta y con ganas de ganar, hablamos con Masai y le dijimos, no cambies a Kado. Porque Kado es el precursor y protagonista de la banda. Él era el Batman, DeMar DeRozan era el Robin. Y lo que veníamos atrás éramos unos unos Big books, enanos que le hacíamos coro. Y como había una buena química, terminan dejando el equipo.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on the impact of Masai Ujiri's trade decisions
quotes.excerpt: That change of Masai, six years later, gives his first title to Toronto Raptors.
quotes.quote: That change of Masai, six years later, gives his first title to Toronto Raptors. Six years later. So you build from the root and many times the fan doesn't see the distant photo, he wants to see the photo here, summed here in the eyes. So look at everything that happened. And until the sun of today, they call me from Toronto, they give me the thanks and I feel that I won the title too. Why? Because we were part of a culture that a winning base was created. And after he ends up changing DeMar DeRozan and brings Kawhi Leonard. Champion. So that, that for me, for me Toronto was a beautiful transformation, I have a lot of affection, for me probably the most delicious city to play, the best fans.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Ese cambio de Masai, seis años después, le da su primer título a Toronto Raptors. Seis años después. Entonces tú construyes desde la raíz y muchas veces el fanático no ve la foto lejana, él quiere ver la foto aquí, sumeada aquí en los ojos. Entonces mira todo lo que pasó. Y hasta el sol de hoy, a mí me llaman de Toronto, me dan las gracias y yo siento que me gané el título también. ¿Por qué? Porque fuimos parte de una cultura que se creó una base ganadora. Y después él termina cambiando a DeMar DeRozan y trae a Kawhi Leonard. Campeón. Entonces eso, eso para mí, para mí Toronto fue una transformación bonita, le tengo mucho cariño, para mí probablemente la ciudad más sabrosa para jugar, los mejores fanáticos.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on the importance of supporting Venezuelan coaches
quotes.excerpt: I have to give more chance to Venezuelan coaches with the Venezuelan selections of older.
quotes.quote: I have to give more chance to Venezuelan coaches with the Venezuelan selections of older. Because it's already good to sign foreigners. And I don't have anything against foreigners, but the first thing has to be yours, second the yours, third the yours, fourth the yours, and fifth the yours. Because if not you are going to invest in paying a foreign coach who does it all the time and does it very well, but you continue stagnating the local coach, the Venezuelan coach. So those are little things that can be improved, that are going to improve from the night to the morning? No. That there is to look for a way to unite, to unify, yes.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Hay que darle más chance a los entrenadores venezolanos con las selecciones venezolanas de mayor. Porque ya está bueno de firmar extranjeros. Y no tengo nada contra los extranjeros, pero lo primero tiene que ser lo tuyo, segundo lo tuyo, tercero lo tuyo, cuarto lo tuyo y quinto lo tuyo. Porque si no tú vas a invertir en pagarle a un entrenador extranjero que lo hace todo el tiempo y lo hace muy bien, pero tú sigues estancando al entrenador local, al entrenador venezolano. Entonces esas son cositas que sí se pudieran mejorar, ¿que se va a mejorar de la noche a la mañana? No. Que hay que buscar una manera de unirnos, de unificarnos, sí.

quotes.speaker: Gravy Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Gravy Vasquez on the importance of investing in youth basketball
quotes.excerpt: We have to improve the structures of minor categories. We have to take out all the associative.
quotes.quote: We have to improve the structures of minor categories. We have to take out all the associative, I agree. We have to give a refreshment to all those associations that don't have prepared leaders, that don't know about the game, that we started this conversation talking about who is the best president of the NBA. Sam Presti, because he is always studying the game. And we in our region have to have that. We are very friendly, very compadre, this is my friend, I leave it here, this is my friend, I leave it here, I get with this and and until we don't change that mentality and we don't pass anything, the market, the fans and the teams today don't dictate where the superstar wants to go.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Hay que mejorar las estructuras de categorías menores. Hay que sacar a todos los asociativos, sí estoy de acuerdo. Hay que darle un refrescamiento a todas esas asociaciones que no tienen dirigentes preparados, que no saben del juego, que empezamos esta conversación hablando de que quién es el mejor presidente de la NBA. Sam Presti, porque siempre está estudiando el juego. Y nosotros en nuestra región tenemos que tener eso. Somos muy amigueros, muy compadre, este es mi amigo, lo dejo aquí, este es mi amigo, lo dejo aquí, me llevo con este y y hasta que nosotros no cambiemos esa mentalidad y no pasamos nada, el mercado, los fanáticos y los equipos hoy en día no dictan a dónde la superestrella quiere ir.

quotes.summary_phrase: Greivis Vasquez evaluates SGA, Jaylen Brown, and Luka Doncic

quotes.quote: I definitely start with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. I love Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. I sit Jaylen Brown on the bench and I cut Luka Doncic. Given how things are right now, Jaylen Brown won. Who thought Jaylen Brown would be doing what he is doing? Rather, I am sitting Jaylen Brown and Jaylen Brown should open because of everything he has done. That question is too imaginative.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Definitivamente inicio con SGA. A mí me encanta SGA. Siento en la banca a Jaylen Brown y corto a Luka Doncic. quotes.summary_phrase: Greivis Vasquez on the impact of Gary Williams

quotes.verbatim_original_language: Ese es Gary Williams, mi papá, el que me ayudó en mi etapa de universidad. Lo amo. El que me dio la pelota y me dio la llave del carro para ser el base que fui y la sensación que fui en el ACC Conference.

quotes.speaker: Greivis Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Greivis Vasquez on the importance of Libertador de Caracas
quotes.excerpt: Libertadores de Caracas is a pillar in my life.
quotes.quote: Libertadores de Caracas is my basketball academy, it is my nursery, looking for a way how I can develop more Venezuelans and Venezuelan coaches. It has not been easy, but Libertadores de Caracas is a pillar in my life.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Esa es mi academia de baloncesto que es mi cantera, buscándole la vuelta cómo puedo desarrollar más venezolanos y entrenadores venezolanos. No ha sido fácil, pero Libertadores de Caracas es un pilar en mi vida.

quotes.summary_phrase: Greivis Vasquez ranks Latin American NBA players
quotes.excerpt: Manu Ginobili is the number one.
quotes.quote: Leandro Barbosa is fifth. Al Horford is third. JJ Barea is fourth. Francisco Garcia is second. And Manu Ginobili is the number one.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Leandro Barbosa quinto. Al Horford tercero. JJ Barea cuarto. Francisco García segundo. Y Manu Ginobili el número uno.

quotes.verbatim_original_language: Mario Chalmers quinto. Jeff Teague cuarto. Brandon Jennings tercero. Jeremy Lin segundo. Y Mike Conley el número uno.

quotes.speaker: Greivis Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Greivis Vasquez on his experience as a backup guard
quotes.excerpt: I was his backup and I thought that I could do better than him as a starter.
quotes.quote: I was his backup and I thought that I could do better than him as a starter. He had OJ Mayo, Tony Allen, Rudy Gay, Zach Randolph, Marc Gasol. And you know what? I realized that was the hardest job and he knew how to handle it, but I did not. It was my rookie year.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Yo era su suplente y yo pensaba que lo podía hacer mejor que él como abridor. Y él tenía OJ Mayo, Tony Allen, Rudy Gay, Zach Randolph, Marc Gasol. Y sabes qué, me di cuenta que ese era el trabajo más difícil y él lo supo manejar, pero yo no. Era mi año de novato.

quotes.speaker: Greivis Vasquez
quotes.summary_phrase: Greivis Vasquez ranks NBA point guards
quotes.excerpt: Chris Paul is the best base of all those I played against.
quotes.quote: Ty Lawson is fifth. Kyle Lowry is fourth. John Wall is third. Chris Paul is the best base of all those I played against. Chris Paul is the best.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Ty Lawson quinto. Kyle Lowry cuarto. John Wall tercero. Chris Paul es el mejor base de todos los que yo jugué en contra. Chris Paul es el mejor.
